draft.title: Stated and implied meanings
card: a meaning said directly in the words. The listener does not have to work it out.
a meaning that is suggested but not said. The listener works it out from the words, the tone and the situation.
Suppose a friend says, "It's nearly nine o'clock." The stated meaning is the time. The implied meaning might be that you should hurry up.
A listener can support a meaning by pointing to words or tone that back it up. A listener can also challenge it by asking what the speaker meant, or by saying the evidence does not fit.
draft.remember: Stated is said outright. Implied is suggested, and a listener can back it up or question it.

a.q: Ravi looks at the messy kitchen and says, "Wow, who left all these dishes?" What is the most likely implied meaning?
opts: He wants someone to wash the dishes
He wants to know who owns the plates
He thinks the kitchen is very small
He is pleased that the dishes are clean
a.why: Ravi does not say "wash them", but his tone and the messy kitchen suggest it. The question about who left them is only the stated surface, so asking for the owner of the plates misses the point.
a.clue: What does Ravi want to happen next?

b.q: Ms Lee tells her class, "The bus leaves at eight sharp." She adds that it will not wait. Zoe replies, "So you are saying we should be early?" What is Zoe doing?
opts: Putting an implied meaning into words to check it
Repeating a meaning that Ms Lee stated directly
Disputing the stated time that the bus leaves
Changing the topic to talk about something else
b.why: Ms Lee stated the time and implied that students should be early. Zoe puts the implied meaning into words to check it. She does not dispute the time, which was the stated meaning.
b.clue: Was being early said directly, or only suggested?

a.best: He wants someone to wash the dishes

b.best: Putting an implied meaning into words to check it

problems.detail: The remember line attaches 'a listener can back it up or question it' only to implied meanings. The card and the chapter point say a listener can support or challenge any meaning, stated or implied, so the line narrows what the card teaches.

check.summary: Both questions are sound, each with one clear right answer. The remember line wrongly suggests that only implied meanings can be supported or challenged, when the card says both stated and implied meanings can be.
